stories.hook: ¿Bloquea el opioide la respuesta antidepresiva de la ketamina?
stories.headline: Naltrexona atenúa la actividad glutamatérgica y la mejoría depresiva inducida por ketamina
stories.finding: En un estudio cruzado doble ciego con 26 pacientes con trastorno depresivo mayor, la administración de 50 mg de naltrexona antes de la infusión de ketamina (0,5 mg/kg) redujo significativamente el aumento del cociente glutamato + glutamina / N‑acetil‑aspartato en la corteza cingulada anterior (F₁,₂₅₃ = 4,83; p = 0,029). Además, la naltrexona atenuó la disminución de la puntuación en la Escala de Depresión de Montgomery‑Åsberg observada al día 1 (interacción condición‑tiempo, F₁,₇₄ = 5,39; p = 0,023).
stories.takeaway: El hallazgo indica que el sistema opioide modula la respuesta aguda de la ketamina, lo que podría guiar estrategias de combinación farmacológica o la selección de pacientes para optimizar la eficacia antidepresiva.
stories.paperTitle: Effect of naltrexone pretreatment on ketamine-induced glutamatergic activity and symptoms of depression: a randomized crossover study
stories.originalAbstract: We investigated the potential role of the opioid system in modulating glutamatergic effects of ketamine administration in major depressive disorder. Twenty-six adults with major depressive disorder participated in a double-blind crossover study, receiving oral placebo or 50 mg naltrexone before an intravenous infusion of 0.5 mg per kg ketamine. Brain glutamatergic activity in the anterior cingulate cortex was measured using functional magnetic resonance spectroscopy and depressive symptoms were assessed with the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale. Naltrexone attenuated the increase in glutamate + glutamine to total N-acetylaspartate ratio during ketamine infusion compared to placebo (F1,253 = 4.83, P = 0.029) and also attenuated the reduction in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale scores on day 1 (condition-by-time interaction, F1,74 = 5.39, P = 0.023). These findings demonstrate that the opioid system modulates the acute response to ketamine and subsequent antidepressant effects. Interactions between the glutamate and opioid systems may have implications for the development of new depression treatment strategies. ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT04977674 .

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención entrenada frenar la rumiación?
stories.headline: La técnica de entrenamiento de atención muestra eficacia general contra la rumiación
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática incluyó 33 estudios de eficacia del ATT y encontró que la técnica es generalmente eficaz para aumentar la conciencia metacognitiva, romper patrones de pensamiento repetitivo y mejorar la flexibilidad ejecutiva en distintas poblaciones. Sin embargo, su efectividad es menor cuando se compara con grupos de control que reciben intervenciones activas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda al ATT como una estrategia breve y basada en evidencia para reducir la rumiación, ofreciendo a los profesionales una herramienta transdiagnóstica que potencia la flexibilidad cognitiva y la distancia metacognitiva de los pensamientos repetitivos.
stories.paperTitle: Üstbilişsel Terapi Stratejisi Olarak Dikkat Eğitimi Tekniğinin Etkililiği: Sistematik Bir Gözden Geçirme
stories.originalAbstract: Dikkat Eğitimi Tekniği (Attention Training Technique – ATT), düşüncelere mesafeli farkındalığı artırmayı, tekrarlayıcı düşünme kalıplarını bozmayı ve yürütücü işlevlerde esnekliği artırmayı amaçlayan kısa süreli bir üstbilişsel terapi stratejisidir. Bu çalışma, söz konusu tekniğin farklı örneklemler üzerindeki etkililiğini değerlendiren araştırmaları sistematik olarak gözden geçirmeyi amaçlamaktadır. Bu kapsamda, “Attention training technique” anahtar kelimesi kullanılarak PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science ve PubMED veri tabanlarında yayımlanmış çalışmalar taranmıştır. Bu gözden geçirme çalışmasına belirli dahil etme kriterlerine dayanarak, toplam 33 etkililik çalışması (söz konusu veri tabanlarından elde edilen 30 ve diğer kaynaklardan 3 çalışma) dâhil edilmiştir. Bulgular; örneklem özellikleri, kontrol ve karşılaştırma koşulları, gruplara atama yöntemleri, ölçüm araçları, ölçüm sıklığı, seans özellikleri, çalışma sonuçları ve yanlılık riskinin değerlendirilmesi temelinde özetlenmiştir. Farklı örneklemler ve bağlamlarda elde edilen sonuçlar, ATT’nin genel olarak etkili olduğunu göstermektedir; ancak bu etkililik, aktif müdahale içeren kontrol gruplarıyla karşılaştırıldığında bazı ölçümlerle sınırlı kalmaktadır. Buna karşın, bekleme listesi veya bir müdahale uygulanmayan kontrol gruplarıyla yapılan karşılaştırmalarda daha belirgin ve anlamlı farklılıklar ortaya çıkmıştır. ATT, temelde üstbilişsel terapinin bir bileşeni olarak değerlendirilse de mevcut kanıtlar bu tekniğin tek başına uygulandığında da etkili olduğunu göstermektedir. Ayrıca, incelenen çalışmalar ATT’nin farklı terapi yaklaşımlarına entegre edilmesiyle de etkili sonuçlar verdiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Bağımsız değerlendiricilerin kullanıldığı, farklı örneklem gruplarının dâhil edildiği, farklı seans sayıları ve değişkenlerin test edildiği, ayrıca daha uzun izlem sürelerinin uygulandığı gelecek araştırmaların, ATT’nin etkililiğine katkı sunacağı düşünülmektedir.

stories.hook: ¿Los genes del sobresalto revelan la ansiedad?
stories.headline: Variantes genéticas del sobresalto se asocian con mayor gravedad de ansiedad
stories.finding: En una muestra de 508 participantes, se analizaron variantes genéticas vinculadas a la respuesta de sobresalto y se encontró evidencia preliminar de que esos alelos se asocian con mayor gravedad de ansiedad en varios trastornos psiquiátricos. El hallazgo sugiere al sobresalto como posible endofenotipo genético de la ansiedad.
stories.takeaway: Identificar variantes genéticas relacionadas con el sobresalto abre la posibilidad de desarrollar biomarcadores para predecir la vulnerabilidad a la ansiedad y orientar intervenciones personalizadas, avanzando la comprensión de los mecanismos biológicos subyacentes.
stories.paperTitle: Genetic Investigation of Physiological Phenotypes to Understand Anxiety Mechanisms
stories.originalAbstract: The role of genetics in the susceptibility for anxiety disorders is widely acknowledged, and research to identify risk factors has advanced to encompass larger genome-wide approaches. However, using diagnoses in genetic studies limits the search to phenotypes that are very heterogeneous with symptoms spanning many domains (e.g., emotion, cognition, behaviour, physiology). The endophenotype concept in psychiatry aims to remedy this complexity by identifying measurable and genetically modulated traits that link genes with disorders. Across the anxiety disorders, heart rate variability (HRV) has evidence for being diminished, and startle reactivity exaggerated. The overall goal of this thesis is to evaluate the endophenotype potential of reduced HRV and heightened startle for anxiety disorders and determine whether their genetics could shed new light on the biology of pathological anxiety. The first project used a hypothesis-driven set of genetic variants previously related to human startle response, finding preliminary evidence for the association of startle variants with anxiety severity across psychiatric disorders (N = 508). The remaining three projects focused on HRV measured remotely with a wearable device in 120 patients with anxiety disorders and 120 healthy controls. The second project of this thesis validated the relationship of reduced resting HRV with anxiety disorders, also finding an association of lower HRV with greater physical anxiety symptoms. The third project supported the existence of a genetic overlap between anxiety disorders and resting HRV using a polygenic risk score approach. This project also identified a subset of the top variants from a large genome-wide study of HRV that show association with anxiety disorders, with some relationships mediated by resting HRV. The final project found evidence for different patterns of anxiety-modulated HRV in patients with anxiety disorders and healthy controls using a newly created virtual reality (VR) paradigm consisting of exposure to anxiety-inducing and neutral VR conditions. These studies add support for HRV and startle as endophenotypes of anxiety disorders, with their genetics potentially aiding the development of novel medication targets. The combination of symptomatology, genetics, and physiology thus enhances our understanding of mechanisms underlying anxiety disorders which may lead to the establishment of more precise treatment regimens.

stories.hook: ¿Los latidos monaurales pueden reducir la ansiedad mejor que la música sola?
stories.headline: Latidos monaurales de baja y moderada intensidad reducen ansiedad más que la música sola
stories.finding: En el estudio 1 con 207 participantes, los grupos con latidos monaurales de baja o moderada intensidad redujeron la ansiedad más que el grupo música‑solo (p = 0.047, β = ‑0.46), mientras que la alta intensidad disminuyó menos la ansiedad que la música‑solo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la incorporación de estímulos auditivos sutiles puede potenciar intervenciones conductuales para la ansiedad, pero que una intensidad excesiva puede contrarrestar el beneficio, orientando el diseño de terapias basadas en música o neurofeedback.
stories.paperTitle: Music with monaural beats for anxiety reduction and mood enhancement in individuals with moderate trait-anxiety
stories.originalAbstract: Monaural beats embedded in music are a popular anxiety-relief intervention, yet implementation parameters and efficacy remain poorly understood. Across two studies of online participants with moderate trait anxiety, we tested whether theta-frequency (4–7 Hz) monaural beats in music produce anxiolytic and mood-enhancing effects beyond the same music alone, whether the salience of the beats relative to the music influences effects, and whether the effect of beats generalizes across heterogeneous musical stimuli. State anxiety, valence and arousal were measured before and after a 25-min listening period. In Study 1, participants (N = 207) were randomly assigned to hear music without beats (Music-Only control) or the same piece with monaural beats blended at three different salience levels: Low-, Moderate-, or High-Beatmix. The Low- and Moderate-Beatmix conditions yielded greater anxiety reductions than Music-Only (p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46, and p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46 respectively), whereas Music-Only reduced anxiety more than the High-Beatmix condition (p adjusted = 0.047, β = 0.42), indicating that overly salient beats might disrupt anxiolytic effects. Time × Condition interactions were not significant for valence or arousal. In Study 2, participants (N = 259) were randomized to one of four stylistically varied tracks, with or without beats at the Moderate-Beatmix level. Averaged across tracks, Beatmix conditions produced greater anxiety reductions (p < 0.0001, β = −0.49) and positive-valence increases (p = 0.029, β = 0.28) than Music-Only. As in Study 1, the Time × Condition interaction was nonsignificant for arousal. These studies provide some of the first evidence that adding monaural beats to music has anxiolytic effects beyond music alone, that efficacy depends on relative beat salience, and that findings replicate across a range of musical tracks.

stories.hook: ¿El abuso emocional infantil aumenta el riesgo de PTSD?
stories.headline: El maltrato emocional infantil se asocia significativamente con PTSD y CPTSD
stories.finding: El metaanálisis incluyó 57 estudios (N=323,776) y encontró una asociación positiva entre el maltrato emocional infantil y los trastornos de estrés postraumático (r=.27, IC 95% [.23, .30]). Los efectos fueron mayores para el abuso emocional (r=.29) que para el abandono emocional (r=.24), aunque la heterogeneidad fue alta (I²=86.5%).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la necesidad de detectar y tratar el maltrato emocional en la infancia, pues su prevención podría reducir significativamente la incidencia de PTSD y CPTSD en la población adulta.
stories.paperTitle: Childhood emotional maltreatment and trauma-related outcomes: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Estimating the association between childhood emotional maltreatment (CEM) and trauma-related outcomes is important for prevention and intervention.Objective: We synthesised the evidence by differentiating between emotional abuse and emotional neglect, examining post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex PTSD (CPTSD) and exploring moderators and mediators.Method: Following PRISMA guidelines, seven databases were searched up to 19/03/2026 (PROSPERO-CRD42024598358) for studies on the association between CEM and PTSD/CPTSD. Study quality was assessed using an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework.Results: Of 11,479 records, 62 were included in the review, of which 57 studies provided 132 effect sizes for a random-effects multilevel meta-analysis (N = 323,776). Study quality was overall fair (Mean NOS = 5.8). A positive association between CEM and PTSD/CPTSD (k = 132, r = .27, 95% CI [.23, .30]) 95% PI [-.04, .53] with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 86.5%). Higher estimates were identified for emotional abuse (k = 71, r = .29, 95% CI [.25, .33]) compared to emotional neglect (k = 55, r = .24, 95% CI [.19, .28]). Effect sizes were similar for CPTSD (k = 29, r = .29, 95% CI [.24, .35]) and PTSD (k = 103, r = .26, 95% CI [.22, .30]). No differences were observed by sex, age, or population type (clinical vs. non-clinical). However, higher estimates were identified in high-income settings and more developed contexts. Narrative synthesis identified cognitive, affective, physiological and interpersonal mechanisms as potential mediators. The certainty of the evidence was generally low. Limitations include the predominance of cross-sectional designs, reliance on self-report measures of CEM and variability across outcome measures.Conclusions: These findings underscore the importance of CEM in trauma-related symptomatology and support the need for its systematic assessment in clinical and research settings, particularly by highlighting differences between emotional abuse and emotional neglect.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el cuerpo mejorar la terapia psicodinámica?
stories.headline: La terapia psicodinámica incorporando el cuerpo reduce síntomas depresivos
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática y meta‑análisis de ensayos controlados aleatorizados encontró que los tratamientos psicodinámicos que integran la experiencia corporal producen una disminución significativa de la sintomatología depresiva en comparación con controles o terapias consolidadas. Los estudios incluidos describen diversas modalidades corporales dentro del marco psicodinámico.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que incorporar la dimensión corporal en la psicoterapia psicodinámica potencia su efectividad contra la depresión, orientando a los clínicos a integrar técnicas somáticas para mejorar los resultados terapéuticos.
stories.paperTitle: Psychodynamic treatments taking an embodied perspective and their effect on depressive symptomatology: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Within a psychodynamic framework multiple theoretical models are offered in the treatment of depression and some of these models also integrate the subjective experience of the body. We give a brief overview of the subjective body in psychodynamic psychotherapies and the evidence regarding the efficacy of psychodynamic treatments addressing the subjective bodily experience in depression. The subsequent review then aimed at identifying the interventions applied within psychodynamic treatments taking an embodied perspective in the treatment of depression while also aggregating findings on their average efficacy. Methods: A systematic review was carried out on RCTs comparing psychodynamic psychotherapy (PDP) addressing the subjective body to control conditions or bona fide therapies, the latter are therapies that have shown their efficacy in a broad context already. Outcomes were analyzed quantitatively using random effects models. The main characteristics of the applied treatment models were summarized narratively from the underlying intervention descriptions. Findings on the treatment models were structured in clusters according to their theoretical embedding. Results: Eleven Trials matched the inclusion criteria with a total of 1,624 patients. Post treatment PDP addressing the subjective body differed from control conditions with a standardized mean difference (SMD) = -0.53 [p = 0.017, 95% CI (-0.97, -0.09), I 2 = 89.12%]. At follow-up differences to control conditions remained to be present with SMD = -1.23 [p = 0.005, 95% CI (-2.10, -0.35), I 2 = 90.35%]. Compared to bona fide therapies no differences were detected post-treatment when applying two-one-sided-tests [SMD = 0.08, p = 0.039, 90% CI (-0.064, 0.23)]. Throughout the applied interventions three overarching technical principles were identified. Concurrently marked differences existed. Conclusion: The findings of our study suggest that PDPs addressing the subjective body are potentially efficacious. However, further conceptual elaboration on embodied treatment techniques is necessary. Subsequent studies should, in addition, scrutinize the contribution that these specific interventions make at the process and outcome level. Systematic review registration: PROSPERO, identifier (CRD42024523337).

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influye la intolerancia al malestar en el juego?
stories.headline: Intolerancia momentánea al malestar y estrategias de regulación predicen mayor duración y frecuencia del juego
stories.finding: En una muestra de 132 adultos australianos, la intolerancia al malestar momentánea se asoció con una mayor duración de la sesión de juego (OR = 1.13, IC 95 % [1.02, 1.25]). Asimismo, el uso de estrategias de regulación emocional maladaptativas incrementó la probabilidad de episodios de juego (OR = 1.24, IC 95 % [1.03, 1.50]).
stories.takeaway: Estos hallazgos sugieren que intervenir la tolerancia al malestar y promover estrategias de regulación adaptativas podría reducir la persistencia y frecuencia del juego problemático en tiempo real.
stories.paperTitle: Exploring real-time associations between momentary distress tolerance, emotion regulation, and gambling behavior in Australian adults: An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study.
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: Guided by the dynamic model of relapse, this study examined whether momentary distress intolerance (DI) and emotion regulation (ER; maladaptive and adaptive strategy use) predict gambling behavior (episodes, expenditure, duration) in real time and whether momentary DI and ER interact with each other and with stable (problem gambling severity, high-risk situations) and momentary (psychological distress, state impulsivity) vulnerabilities in predicting gambling episodes. METHOD: A secondary analysis was conducted on an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study comprising a pre-EMA survey of stable variables followed by a 28-day period of twice-daily smartphone-delivered EMAs of momentary variables and gambling episodes. The convenience sample included 132 Australian adults (Mage = 29.9 years; 58.3% male; 94.7% endorsed gambling problems) who reported gambling in a typical month. RESULTS: Mixed-effects logistic regression analyses showed that momentary DI was associated with longer subsequent gambling duration (OR = 1.13, 95% CI [1.02, 1.25], p = .024), and maladaptive ER strategies were associated with both gambling episodes (OR = 1.24, 95% CI [1.03, 1.50], p = .023) and longer subsequent gambling duration (OR = 1.64, 95% CI [1.02, 2.65], p = .042). Adaptive ER strategy use was not significantly associated with gambling behavior. Only DI interacted with state impulsivity (OR = 1.11, 95% CI [1.03, 1.19], p = .005), whereby individuals with low impulsivity were more likely to gamble when DI was low, whereas those with high impulsivity were more likely to gamble when DI was high. CONCLUSIONS: These findings contribute to our understanding of DI and ER strategy use as dynamic, momentary vulnerabilities for gambling behavior and highlight their potential as real-time intervention targets, particularly for individuals with high impulsivity. stories.hook: ¿El sueño materno influye en el desarrollo infantil?
stories.headline: Sueño materno durante el embarazo predice trastornos del sueño infantil
stories.finding: En un estudio prospectivo de 193 madres, se observó que mayores problemas de sueño durante el embarazo se asociaron con más trastornos del sueño y desregulación en los infantes a los 12 meses, incluso después de controlar variables como sexo, edad y ingresos familiares.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la importancia de intervenciones de sueño prenatal para prevenir problemas de regulación en el desarrollo infantil.
stories.paperTitle: The association between maternal sleep and circadian rhythms during pregnancy and infant sleep and socioemotional outcomes
stories.originalAbstract: Studies have established that maternal sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances during pregnancy are associated with poor prenatal and perinatal outcomes for mothers and offspring. However, little work has explored its effects on infant sleep or socioemotional outcomes. The current study examined the relationship between maternal sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances during pregnancy and infant sleep and socioemotional outcomes in a diverse sample of N=193 mothers and their infants (51% White; 52% Female; Mage= 11.95 months). Maternal sleep and circadian rhythms during pregnancy were assessed using self-reports and actigraphy. Mothers reported on infants’ sleep and socioemotional outcomes when infants were one year old. When controlling for infant sex, age, gestational age at birth, and family income-to-needs, mothers who reported more sleep problems during pregnancy had infants with more sleep disturbances and dysregulation (e.g., increased feeding difficulties, sensory sensitivities) when they were one year old. Moreover, mothers who had later sleep timing (i.e., went to bed and woke up later, measured via actigraphy) during pregnancy had infants with more dysregulation and externalizing problems, and mothers with increased intra-daily variability in rest-activity rhythms (as measured via actigraphy) had infants with more externalizing problems. Findings suggest that maternal sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances during pregnancy may be a risk factor for infant sleep problems and socioemotional difficulties.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia ACT mejorar la salud mental del corazón?
stories.headline: ACT reduce significativamente depresión, ansiedad y estrés, y aumenta autocompasión en pacientes cardiacos
stories.finding: En un ensayo clínico aleatorizado, la ACT redujo significativamente depresión, ansiedad y estrés, y aumentó la autocompasión y la regulación emocional en pacientes cardiovasculares. Los tamaños de efecto parciales η² fueron 0,61–0,66 para estas variables.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo muestra que una intervención basada en mindfulness y aceptación puede aliviar el sufrimiento psicológico y potenciar recursos internos en pacientes con enfermedad cardíaca, lo que sugiere su incorporación en la atención integral cardiovascular.
stories.paperTitle: Effectiveness of acceptance and commitment therapy for distress, emotion regulation, and self-compassion in patients with cardiovascular disease: a randomized clinical trial
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular patients experience various psychological problems due to the conditions caused by their disease, making it worse if left untreated. The purpose of the current study was to evaluate the effects of acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) on distress, emotion regulation, and self-compassion in patients with cardiovascular disease. METHODS: This study was a randomized clinical trial with pre-test, post-test, and 2-month and 4-month follow-up periods accompanying a control group and an experimental group. Patients filled out questionnaires at four stages; a Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-21), an Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ), and a Self-Compassion Scale (SCS). The experimental group underwent a treatment protocol based on ACT. Data were then analyzed using SPSS-25 with repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). RESULTS: ACT significantly reduced depression, anxiety, and stress, enhanced self-compassion, and improved emotion regulation in cardiac patients. Between-subjects (group) partial Eta squared (η²) for depression, anxiety, stress, reappraisal, suppression, and self-compassion were 0.61, 0.64, 0.66, 0.62, 0.66, and 0.65, respectively. Treatment efficacy was maintained at the 2-month and 6-month follow-up visits. CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that treating cardiac patients' psychological problems in an ACT-focused manner may have an impact on how well they respond to their treatment.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la inteligencia espiritual proteger contra el perfeccionismo tóxico?
stories.headline: El perfeccionismo maladaptativo aumenta el burnout académico y deteriora la salud mental
stories.finding: El estudio reveló que el perfeccionismo maladaptativo se asoció positivamente con el burnout académico (r=0.51) y con problemas de salud mental (r=0.58); la inteligencia espiritual se analizó como posible mediador de estas relaciones.
stories.takeaway: Comprender que el perfeccionismo tóxico alimenta el agotamiento y el malestar mental sugiere que intervenciones que fortalezcan la inteligencia espiritual podrían mitigar estos efectos y mejorar la resiliencia estudiantil.
stories.paperTitle: The Relationship Between Maladaptive Perfectionism and Academic Burnout with Students’ Mental Health: The Mediating Role of Spiritual Intelligence
stories.journal: Journal of Adolescent and Youth Psychological Studies (JAYPS)
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between maladaptive perfectionism and academic burnout with students’ mental health through the mediating role of spiritual intelligence. Methods and Materials: This study was conducted using a descriptive-correlational design based on structural equation modeling. The statistical population included all high school students in Tehran during the 2025–2026 academic year. A total of 412 students were selected through multistage cluster random sampling. Data were collected using the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory–Student Survey, General Health Questionnaire-28, and Spiritual Intelligence Self-Report Inventory. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated using SPSS-27 software, and structural equation modeling was performed using AMOS-24. The significance of indirect effects was examined using the bootstrap method. Findings: The findings demonstrated that maladaptive perfectionism had a significant positive relationship with academic burnout (r = 0.51, p < 0.01) and mental health problems (r = 0.58, p < 0.01). Academic burnout was also positively associated with mental health problems (r = 0.61, p < 0.01). In contrast, spiritual intelligence showed significant negative relationships with maladaptive perfectionism (r = -0.46, p < 0.01), academic burnout (r = -0.49, p < 0.01), and mental health problems (r = -0.55, p < 0.01). Structural equation modeling indicated that maladaptive perfectionism directly predicted mental health problems (β = 0.37, p < 0.001), while academic burnout also had a significant direct effect on mental health problems (β = 0.41, p < 0.001). Spiritual intelligence significantly mediated the relationships between maladaptive perfectionism, academic burnout, and mental health. The proposed model demonstrated acceptable fit indices (χ²/df = 2.31, CFI = 0.94, TLI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.057). Conclusion: The findings suggest that maladaptive perfectionism and academic burnout are important psychological risk factors negatively influencing students’ mental health, whereas spiritual intelligence serves as a protective psychological resource that reduces emotional distress and improves psychological well-being.

stories.hook: ¿El estilo autoritario aumenta el burnout de enfermeras jóvenes?
stories.headline: Liderazgo autoritario eleva burnout mediante clima organizacional y capital psicológico
stories.finding: En una encuesta transversal con 1,160 enfermeras jóvenes en China, el liderazgo autoritario mostró una correlación positiva significativa con el burnout (r = 0.502, p < 0.01). El clima organizacional y el capital psicológico mediaron esa relación en cadena (β = 0.061, IC 95 % 0.038‑0.086).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir en el estilo de liderazgo y fortalecer el clima organizacional y el capital psicológico puede reducir el desgaste ocupacional en enfermeras jóvenes, mejorando la calidad de atención y la retención del personal.
stories.paperTitle: The effect of authoritarian leadership on young nurses' burnout: the mediating role of organizational climate and psychological capital
stories.originalAbstract: AIM: To investigate the relationship between authoritarian leadership and burnout for young nurses in China and the mediating role of organizational climate and psychological capital in this relationship. BACKGROUND: As the backbone of clinical nursing, young nurses are prone to job burnout due to the tedious work and the intense work intensity of clinical nursing. It is critical to pay close attention to young nurse burnout to elevate nursing quality and patient satisfaction. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was carried out. From November to December 2022, 1,160 nurses from 4 hospitals in Henan, China participated in the survey. Pearson correlation analysis, descriptive statistics and structural equation model were used to analyze the existing data. RESULTS: Authoritarian leadership (r = 0.502, P < 0.01) has a significant positive correlation with burnout, while organizational climate (r = -0.556, P < 0.01) and psychological capital (r = -0.538, P < 0.01) show significant negative correlations with burnout. Organizational climate and psychological capital serve as a chain mediating role between authoritarian leadership and burnout (β = 0.061, 95% CI (0.038, 0.086)). The total effect of authoritarian leadership on burnout (0.297) includes direct effect (0.338) and indirect effect (-0.042). CONCLUSIONS: Organizational climate and psychological capital play a chain mediating role in the relationship between authoritarian leadership and burnout. The results show that nursing managers need to fully understand the disadvantages of authoritarian leadership, adjust relevant behaviors in time, and learn to care for and respect employees. Additionally, from the hospital's organizational climate and young nurses' psychological capital, the implementation of targeted management measures to alleviate nurses' burnout and improve the quality of nursing service.

stories.hook: ¿Qué factores predicen el divorcio a largo plazo?
stories.headline: Predictores individuales, de pareja y socioeconómicos explican el divorcio en 12 años
stories.finding: En una cohorte de 368 parejas heterosexuales recién casadas, se midieron seis grupos de predictores en los seis meses iniciales. Doce años después, el 39 % se divorció; los modelos estructurales bayesianos revelaron que factores individuales, de comportamiento adaptativo y socioeconómicos superaron a la comunicación como predictores.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo amplía la comprensión del divorcio al integrar variables individuales y contextuales, sugiriendo que las intervenciones preventivas deben ir más allá de la comunicación de pareja e incluir apoyo a vulnerabilidades personales y condiciones socioeconómicas.
stories.paperTitle: Individual, interpersonal, and socioeconomic predictors of divorce: A 12-year prospective study.
stories.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
stories.originalAbstract: Divorce is among the most common and costly life disruptions adults may face. Maladaptive and ineffective couple communication is routinely implicated in leading models as the cause of divorce, and interventions designed to prevent divorce accordingly prioritize changes in couple interaction patterns. Yet research linking couple communication to divorce has been inconsistent, and failures of communication-based interventions highlight the need for an expanded view of early signs of risk. Alternative perspectives on divorce draw attention to the vulnerabilities individuals bring into marriage and the socioeconomic circumstances couples must navigate once married, yet the predictive power of these perspectives has never been directly compared to the behavioral model. The current analyses address this gap through a study of 368 different-sex newlywed couples who provided data on six clusters of predictors within 6 months of marriage: relationship satisfaction for each spouse, individual vulnerabilities for each spouse, couples' adaptive behavior, and socioeconomic risk. Over the next 12 years, 39% of couples divorced. Preregistered Bayesian structural equation models and survival analyses demonstrated that each baseline risk factor independently predicted divorce in the expected direction. When all predictors were included simultaneously, only wives' individual vulnerabilities predicted divorce. Adaptive communication behaviors attenuated the risk conferred by wives' vulnerabilities. The best performing model explained 34% of variance in divorce, suggesting that at least one third of couples' divorce risk is detectable early in marriage. Exploring vulnerabilities and their effects promises to deepen understanding of how relationships develop and deteriorate and can clarify boundary conditions of behavioral models of divorce. stories.hook: ¿Qué impulsa la toxicidad entre compañeros en juegos online?
stories.headline: Empatía reduce y apego al personaje aumenta la toxicidad intra‑equipo
stories.finding: En una encuesta a 548 jugadores chinos de MOBA, la empatía afectiva disminuyó la tendencia a dañar a los compañeros, mientras que el apego al personaje la incrementó. Tres procesos de desenganche moral median estas relaciones.
stories.takeaway: Comprender estos mecanismos permite diseñar intervenciones y mecánicas de juego que fomenten la empatía y reduzcan el desenganche moral, mejorando la convivencia y salud mental de los jugadores.
stories.paperTitle: Why do teammates hurt me? Uncovering affective and cognitive mechanisms of intra-team toxic behavior in multiplayer online battle arena
stories.originalAbstract: Toxic behavior is pervasive in the multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) and poses a threat to building a civil online environment. While considerable scholarly attention has been devoted to understanding the factors that predict toxic behavior, there is a paucity of research that focuses on intra-team toxic behavior and comprehensively examines its psychological occurrence mechanism from affective and cognitive aspects. To address these gaps, the present research investigates the influence of affective empathy, character attachment, and moral disengagement on intra-team toxic behavior. Findings from a survey of 548 Chinese MOBA players indicated that the propensity to hurt teammates can be weakened by affective empathy but exacerbated by character attachment. Moreover, three mechanisms of moral disengagement mediate the relationships between affective empathy, character attachment, and intra-team toxic behavior. The research offered theoretical insights into toxic behavior and gameplay studies, while also suggesting design improvements for MOBA.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la evaluación social alterar nuestro esfuerzo mental?
stories.headline: La evaluación social incrementa el esfuerzo mental en conflictos de decisión
stories.finding: El estudio demostró que superar un conflicto entre respuestas Pavlovianas e instrumentales genera un esfuerzo mental mensurable mediante pupillometría. Además, la presencia de evaluación social, a diferencia de la mera presencia, perturba específicamente los mecanismos de generación de acción y procesamiento de recompensas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la presión social puede modificar la carga cognitiva y los circuitos de recompensa, lo que es crucial para diseñar intervenciones que mitiguen decisiones impulsivas en contextos grupales o clínicos.
stories.paperTitle: Biases in individual and social decision-making
stories.journal: Elektronische Hochschulschriften der LMU München (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München)
stories.originalAbstract: Human behavior is shaped by the interplay between innate response tendencies and experience–dependent learning. Automatic Pavlovian reactions, i.e. approach to potential rewards and inhibition in the face of potential punishments, often facilitate rapid, adaptive action, yet they can conflict with instrumental demands that require acting (or withholding action) contrary to these biases. This thesis investigates how such biases shape learning and decision–making and how social contexts modulate their expression. A central theme is that overcoming Pavlovian–instrumental conflict carries measurable mental effort, and that social evaluation selectively perturbs the mechanisms supporting action generation and reward processing. I take a behavioral, physiological and computational approach to (i) formalize Pavlovian–instrumental interactions in reinforcement learning, (ii) quantify the mental effort involved in decision–making under incongruency using pupillometry and (iii) dissociate the effects of mere social presence and social evaluation on learning. First, I synthesize prior theoretical and empirical work to motivate a reinforcement learning framework in which Pavlovian value signals invigorate or suppress action independently of instrumental contingencies, while frontal control processes can down–regulate these influences when they are maladaptive. Within this framework, I derive testable predictions linking latent variables (action values, prediction errors, and Pavlovian conflict) to both behavior choices, reaction times) and trial–by–trial task–evoked pupillary responses as a proxy for arousal/effort. I then test these predictions in a Go/NoGo learning paradigm that orthogonalizes action requirements (Go vs. NoGo) and outcome valence (reward vs. punishment). Across seven candidate reinforcement learning models, variants that include a Pavlovian component (reward→invigoration, punishment→inhibition) best explain human behavior, and the simplest of these, with a single outcome sensitivity and a learned Pavlovian value, wins; model and parameter recovery confirm that this conclusion is identifiable. Behaviorally, participants are more accurate under congruent mappings (rewarded actions and preventive inactions) than under incongruent ones (omission schedule and active avoidance), with the omission schedule particularly impaired, and respond faster for reward than for punishment. Physiologically, the task-evoked pupil response differentiates trial types by Pavlovian–instrumental congruence at the cue, by the executed action at the decision, and by losses and omitted rewards at the outcome. Time–resolved model–based analyses ground these effects in the latent variables of the winning model: the learned Pavlovian value scales the pupil during cue evaluation and drives dilation at the decision when it opposes the required action, while an unsigned Pavlovian prediction error, i.e. surprise irrespective of its sign, governs the outcome–locked response. At every stage the pupil tracks the Pavlovian rather than the instrumental quantity, linking latent learning signals to physiological effort. To assess social modulation, I repeat the task within subjects across three contexts: individual performance, passive social presence and active social evaluation with contingent payoffs. Social evaluation produces a selective deficit in action learning: participants show impaired acquisition and execution of Go responses while NoGo learning remains intact. Concomitantly, phasic pupillary responses associated with action requirements are attenuated under evaluation, consistent with a reduction in available cognitive resources or altered noradrenergic arousal when decisions are made under social judgment. Despite stable average Pavlovian and Go biases across contexts, evaluation shifts Positivity bias (reward vs. avoidance performance) toward negative values, indicating a conservative reweighting of reward processing in evaluative settings. Together, these findings provide a unified account of how Pavlovian biases shape human learning and choice, how cognitive control overcomes these biases at measurable physiological cost, and how social evaluation selectively disrupts action generation and reward processing. The work clarifies the computational roles of Pavlovian and instrumental systems, grounds the pupil response in model–derived variables resolved across the course of a decision, and isolates social evaluation, distinct from mere presence, as a driver of action–specific learning impairments. Limitations include the interpretive specificity of pupillometry and the need to generalize beyond the Go/NoGo domain; I outline multi–method extensions (EEG/fMRI/pharmacology) and broader decision paradigms (risk, delay, effort). Overall, the thesis advances a testable framework for understanding when and why humans fail to act optimally, even when they “know better”, and how social environments can tip the balance between reflexive and goal–directed control.

First, I synthesize prior theoretical and empirical work to motivate a reinforcement learning framework in which Pavlovian value signals invigorate or suppress action independently of instrumental contingencies, while frontal control processes can down–regulate these influences when they are maladaptive. Within this framework, I derive testable predictions linking latent variables (action values, prediction errors, and Pavlovian conflict) to both behavior choices, reaction times) and trial–by–trial task–evoked pupillary responses as a proxy for arousal/effort. I then test these predictions in a Go/NoGo learning paradigm that orthogonalizes action requirements (Go vs. NoGo) and outcome valence (reward vs. punishment). Across seven candidate reinforcement learning models, variants that include a Pavlovian component (reward→invigoration, punishment→inhibition) best explain human behavior, and the simplest of these, with a single outcome sensitivity and a learned Pavlovian value, wins; model and parameter recovery confirm that this conclusion is identifiable. Behaviorally, participants are more accurate under congruent mappings (rewarded actions and preventive inactions) than under incongruent ones (omission schedule and active avoidance), with the omission schedule particularly impaired, and respond faster for reward than for punishment. Physiologically, the task-evoked pupil response differentiates trial types by Pavlovian–instrumental congruence at the cue, by the executed action at the decision, and by losses and omitted rewards at the outcome. Time–resolved model–based analyses ground these effects in the latent variables of the winning model: the learned Pavlovian value scales the pupil during cue evaluation and drives dilation at the decision when it opposes the required action, while an unsigned Pavlovian prediction error, i.e. surprise irrespective of its sign, governs the outcome–locked response. At every stage the pupil tracks the Pavlovian rather than the instrumental quantity, linking latent learning signals to physiological effort. To assess social modulation, I repeat the task within subjects across three contexts: individual performance, passive social presence and active social evaluation with contingent payoffs. Social evaluation produces a selective deficit in action learning: participants show impaired acquisition and execution of Go responses while NoGo learning remains intact. Concomitantly, phasic pupillary responses associated with action requirements are attenuated under evaluation, consistent with a reduction in available cognitive resources or altered noradrenergic arousal when decisions are made under social judgment. Despite stable average Pavlovian and Go biases across contexts, evaluation shifts Positivity bias (reward vs. avoidance performance) toward negative values, indicating a conservative reweighting of reward processing in evaluative settings. Together, these findings provide a unified account of how Pavlovian biases shape human learning and choice, how cognitive control overcomes these biases at measurable physiological cost, and how social evaluation selectively disrupts action generation and reward processing. The work clarifies the computational roles of Pavlovian and instrumental systems, grounds the pupil response in model–derived variables resolved across the course of a decision, and isolates social evaluation, distinct from mere presence, as a driver of action–specific learning impairments. Limitations include the interpretive specificity of pupillometry and the need to generalize beyond the Go/NoGo domain; I outline multi–method extensions (EEG/fMRI/pharmacology) and broader decision paradigms (risk, delay, effort). Overall, the thesis advances a testable framework for understanding when and why humans fail to act optimally, even when they “know better”, and how social environments can tip the balance between reflexive and goal–directed control.

stories.hook: ¿Los rasgos obsesivo‑compulsivos predisponen al duelo prolongado?
stories.headline: Rasgos obsesivo‑compulsivos aumentan riesgo de trastorno de duelo prolongado
stories.finding: El estudio con 585 adultos reveló que los rasgos de personalidad obsesivo‑compulsiva se asociaron con mayor sensación de irrealidad, cogniciones de duelo y evitación, los cuales a su vez predijeron síntomas de duelo prolongado, confirmando el modelo propuesto.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que evaluar rasgos obsesivo‑compulsivos puede identificar a personas vulnerables al duelo prolongado, orientando intervenciones preventivas y terapéuticas centradas en la regulación cognitiva y la reducción de la evitación.
stories.paperTitle: Obsessive compulsive personality traits as a risk factor for prolonged grief disorder
stories.originalAbstract: This study aimed to propose and test a model explaining the relationship between obsessive-compulsive personality traits (OCPT) and prolonged grief disorder (PGD) symptoms through the cognitive-behavioral conceptualization of Boelen and colleagues. In the proposed theoretical model, it was expected that obsessive-compulsive personality traits would be associated with experienced unrealness, grief cognitions, and avoidance which will result in a relationship with prolonged grief symptoms. The participants of the present study consisted of 585 individuals aged between 18 and 65 years who had lost a loved one through death. Participants who had lost a loved one more than 5 years ago were not included in the study. The convenience sampling method was used, and data was collected online. The measurement tools were the Pathological Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Scale (POPS), Prolonged Grief Scale Revised (PG-13-R), Grief Cognitions Questionnaire (GCQ), Depressive and Anxious Avoidance in Prolonged Grief Questionnaire (DAAPGQ), and Experienced Unrealness Scale (EUS). Analyses were conducted using the SPSS AMOS software. The results revealed that the proposed model, which explains the relationship between OCPT and PGD through unrealness of experience, grief cognitions, and anxious avoidance, was supported. These findings provide empirical evidence for the significant impact of personality traits shaping the way individuals grieve.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el ejercicio aeróbico mejorar la función ejecutiva en niños con TDAH?
stories.headline: Ejercicio aeróbico no muestra evidencia clara de mejora ejecutiva en TDAH infantil
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática y meta‑análisis de nueve ensayos controlados aleatorizados evaluó el efecto del ejercicio aeróbico sobre la función ejecutiva en niños con TDAH de 6 a 12 años. Los resultados no aportaron evidencia sustancial de mejora significativa tras la intervención.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que, pese al interés clínico, el ejercicio aeróbico aún no cuenta con respaldo empírico sólido para potenciar la función ejecutiva en TDAH, orientando a los profesionales a priorizar intervenciones con evidencia comprobada.
stories.paperTitle: Effect of aerobic exercise on the improvement of executive function in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: Aerobic exercise (AE) interventions are beginning to be used as an emerging adjunctive treatment modality in the treatment of children with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). However, to date, there is no substantial evidence to support the improved effects of aerobic exercise intervention in children with ADHD aged 6-12 years. This study aims to investigate the effect of aerobic exercise therapy on executive function in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder aged 6-12 years. Method: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis using PubMed and Web of Science. The cut-off date was June 1, 2023. The aim was to assess the impact of aerobic exercise interventions on children with ADHD and all randomized controlled trials eligible for aerobic exercise interventions for children with ADHD were included. Nine randomized controlled trials were screened for eligibility for systematic evaluation, and the nine studies were assessed for risk of bias using the PEDro score and the GRADE Quality of Evidence Evaluation System for quality grading of outcome indicators. After testing for heterogeneity, a random-effects model was selected for analysis. Finally, meta-analyses and regression analyses were performed on the core functions (inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory) and subgroups of the nine studies on executive function using Revman 5.4 and Stata 16.0. Results: The risk of bias evaluation showed a mean PEDro score of 7.78, and of the nine studies, two were rated as having excellent methodological quality, while the remaining seven had a good level of evidence, and the GRADE evidence evaluation showed that the outcome indicators were all of moderate quality. Inhibitory control [SMD = 0.83,95% CI (0.37-1.29), Z = 3.51, p = 0.0005], cognitive flexibility [SMD = 0.65,95% CI (0.37-0.93), Z = 4.58, p < 0.00001], and working memory [SMD = 0.48,95% CI (0.02-0.95), Z = 2.03, p = 0.04] were statistically significant, with effect sizes of moderate or higher; furthermore, in subgroup analyses type of intervention, duration, intensity, and medication use had different effects on inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility, and the combined IC, CF statistic found that a single category of aerobic exercise ( β = 0.867, p < 0.001), moderate intensity ( β = 0.928, p < 0.001), 6-12 weeks (β = 0.804, p < 0.001), 60-90 min ( β = 0.894, p < 0.001), and the use of medication ( β = 1.202, p = 0.002) were better for overall improvement in EF. Conclusion: Aerobic exercise therapy significantly improved executive functioning in children with ADHD, showing above moderate effect sizes especially in inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory. Aerobic exercise therapy can be used as a reference in improving executive function in children with ADHD, but given the limitations of this study, it should be used with caution when applied in clinical settings.

stories.headline: Revisión sistemática revela cuatro pilares universales de la cohesión familiar
stories.finding: El análisis de 41 estudios entre 2015 y 2023 identificó cuatro dimensiones clave de la cohesión familiar: vínculo emocional, adaptabilidad, comunicación y apoyo. Además, se observaron patrones comunes y mecanismos específicos de cada cultura que potencian la cohesión.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a profesionales y políticas a diseñar intervenciones que refuercen esas cuatro dimensiones, adaptándolas a contextos culturales, para promover el desarrollo integral y la resiliencia de los niños.
stories.paperTitle: Strengthening Family Bonds: A Systematic Review of Factors and Interventions That Enhance Family Cohesion
stories.originalAbstract: Strong emotional bonds within families are foundational to children’s academic, psychological, and social development. While family cohesion is widely recognized as a protective factor across these domains, there remains a need to understand the specific mechanisms and interventions that foster such cohesion, particularly in diverse socioeconomic and cultural contexts. This systematic review examines global evidence on factors influencing family cohesion and evaluates intervention strategies designed to strengthen familial relationships. Drawing on 41 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2023, this review adheres to PRISMA guidelines and applies the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) to assess methodological quality. The findings are organized around four core dimensions of family cohesion—emotional bonding, adaptability, communication, and support—and highlight both common patterns and culturally specific mechanisms. Studies were drawn from a range of settings including North America, sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, East and Southeast Asia, and Europe, enabling a cross-cultural analysis of how family cohesion operates under different social, cultural, and economic conditions. Intervention strategies are reviewed separately following the synthesis of correlations, with attention to their effectiveness, cultural relevance, and contextual adaptability. Community-based programs, trauma-informed therapies, and parenting interventions emerge as key approaches, though their success has varied by regional and structural context. Studies consistently demonstrate that higher family cohesion correlates with improved academic outcomes, as supportive home environments promote motivation, reduce stress, and enhance learning. Mental health benefits are also evident, with cohesive and adaptable families mitigating risks of anxiety and depression through open communication and emotional availability. Social competence is fostered through observed and practiced interpersonal skills within family settings. Socioeconomic status emerges as both a challenge and a moderating factor, with lower-SES families facing greater barriers to cohesion but also displaying notable resilience when supported through external interventions. Effective strategies identified include family therapy, parenting education, community-based programs, culturally sensitive approaches, and socioeconomic policy supports. Family cohesion and adaptability are critical to nurturing children’s academic success, emotional well-being, and social development. This review contributes to a more culturally nuanced and policy-relevant understanding of family cohesion by integrating empirical findings across global contexts and identifying both shared and differentiated pathways to resilience. The results inform future program design and suggest priorities for cross-cultural family research and intervention development.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la eritropoyetina mejorar la plasticidad sináptica?
stories.headline: La eritropoyetina reduce la inhibición de interneuronas hipocampales
stories.finding: El estudio analizó aproximadamente 12 000 núcleos de células individuales del hipocampo de ratón, identificando 15 subtipos de interneuronas. La administración de eritropoyetina recombinante disminuyó la complejidad dendrítica, la conectividad sináptica y la plasticidad de poblaciones específicas de interneuronas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la eritropoyetina podría restaurar el equilibrio excitatorio‑inhibitorio y potenciar la plasticidad sináptica, ofreciendo una vía potencial para tratar trastornos psiquiátricos asociados a disfunciones de interneuronas, como esquizofrenia o autismo.
stories.paperTitle: Erythropoietin restrains the inhibitory potential of interneurons in the mouse hippocampus
stories.originalAbstract: Severe psychiatric illnesses, for instance schizophrenia, and affective diseases or autism spectrum disorders, have been associated with cognitive impairment and perturbed excitatory-inhibitory balance in the brain. Effects in juvenile mice can elucidate how erythropoietin (EPO) might aid in rectifying hippocampal transcriptional networks and synaptic structures of pyramidal lineages, conceivably explaining mitigation of neuropsychiatric diseases. An imminent conundrum is how EPO restores synapses by involving interneurons. By analyzing ~12,000 single-nuclei transcriptomic data, we generated a comprehensive molecular atlas of hippocampal interneurons, resolved into 15 interneuron subtypes. Next, we studied molecular alterations upon recombinant human (rh)EPO and saw that gene expression changes relate to synaptic structure, trans-synaptic signaling and intracellular catabolic pathways. Putative ligand-receptor interactions between pyramidal and inhibitory neurons, regulating synaptogenesis, are altered upon rhEPO. An array of in/ex vivo experiments confirms that specific interneuronal populations exhibit reduced dendritic complexity, synaptic connectivity, and changes in plasticity-related molecules. Metabolism and inhibitory potential of interneuron subgroups are compromised, leading to greater excitability of pyramidal neurons. To conclude, improvement by rhEPO of neuropsychiatric phenotypes may partly owe to restrictive control over interneurons, facilitating re-connectivity and synapse development.
